name: Neural Factorization Machines (NFMs)
description: Neural Factorization Machine (NFM) is a novel model proposed for prediction in sparse settings. It seamlessly combines the linearity of Factorization Machines (FMs) when modeling second-order feature interactions, with the non-linearity characteristic of neural networks when modeling higher-order feature interactions. Conceptually, NFM is more expressive than FM because FM can be viewed as a special case of NFM that lacks hidden layers. Empirically, NFM significantly outperforms FM on two regression tasks, showing a 7.3% relative improvement with just one hidden layer. Furthermore, compared to recent deep learning methods like Wide&Deep and DeepCross, NFM offers better performance while utilizing a shallower structure, making it much easier to train and tune in practice.
